rationale: The contract expressly withholds source, launch clock and input timing. Direct sampling may be timing-closed synchronous data or an unsafe asynchronous input; the port name establishes neither.
caveats: Obtain integration source/timing/clock relationship, startup/reset and consumer contracts. Fit as a deliberate unknown-premise test despite sharing the direct-sample topology with C02/C13. It must not be scored as a proven asynchronous defect.

author_reading.evidence_and_limits: Keep unresolved pending integrator source, timing, reset and mode contract. The port name is not evidence.

labels.rationale: A directly captured input is not intrinsically asynchronous. Its launch domain, timing relationship and reset/startup contract are unavailable, so neither a synchronous safe input nor an unsynchronized asynchronous input can be established.
labels.caveats: Close with the integration source/launch clock, relationship to clk_d, input timing/stability and startup/reset guarantees, and receiving-use contract. A synchronous timing-closed source can make the site good; an independent changing source with no downstream containment makes it bad. Do not infer a domain from async_in.

labels.rationale: Contract line 7 expressly withholds source domain and timing. The identical one-flop topology is safe if the input is synchronous and meets timing, unsafe for an unconstrained asynchronous source. Neither is established; async_in naming supplies no evidence.
labels.caveats: Source/reset/timing integration facts must be obtained before assigning a safe or unsafe crossing. Duplicates C02/C13 structurally while deliberately changing known boundary premises. No whole-IP clean-control claim is supported.
